jobs.description:
About Us 

Hawk is the leading provider of AI-supported anti-money laundering and fraud detection technology. Banks and payment providers globally are using Hawk’s powerful combination of traditional rules and explainable AI to improve the effectiveness of their AML compliance and fraud prevention by identifying more crime while maximizing efficiency by reducing false positives. With our solution, we are playing a vital role in the global fight against Money Laundering, Fraud, or the financing of terrorism. We offer a culture of mutual trust, support and passion – while providing individuals with opportunities to grow professionally and make a difference in the world. 

Your Mission

As an Implementation Specialist at Hawk, your responsibility is to transform customer requirements into a functioning solution that helps them achieve their business objectives around transaction monitoring, customer screening and fraud detection, alongside cutting-edge AI technologies. You start with a signed contract and support the customer until go-live. This includes translating policies, regulatory obligations and risk factors into Hawk's setup, data mapping, workflow configuration, UAT support and ensuring that key project timelines and milestones are met. You support our customers in realising true value by detecting more financial crime, allowing investigators to focus on what matters instead of drowning in false positives, and adopting state-of-the-art AI technologies.

Key Responsibilities

  • Requirements and needs assessment: gather and analyse the customer's AML, fraud and screening requirements and advise on best-practice configuration.

  • Configuration: translate policies, screening algorithms, regulatory requirements and risk factors into Hawk's setup, covering rules, screening, customer risk rating and workflows.

  • Data mapping and integration: lead the technical deployment and integration with the customer's systems, via API or batch mechanisms.

  • Testing and go-live: support the customer through testing, UAT and sign-off, troubleshoot issues, and support a successful transition to a production environment.

  • Training and enablement: deliver training to the customer's teams from a functional as well as technical standpoint.

  • Project management: plan and run the implementation from signature to go-live on time and within scope, with documentation and regular stakeholder updates, combining hands-on work with project leadership.

  • Primary contact: be the first point of contact for implementation questions and issues.

  • Collaboration and feedback: work closely with Customer Value Partners for a smooth implementation, and bring actionable customer feedback and gaps to Product, Development and Hawk's GTM organisation.

  • Document every configuration decision and the reasoning behind it, so the setup holds up when the customer's auditor or regulator asks why a rule was set the way it was.

  • Manage each implementation task and the implementation success as an outcome you own, as directed by our Customer Value Partner, resulting in activity completion and a go-live on the dates you committed to.

Your Profile

  • 6+ years in implementation consulting or solution consulting, with at least 3 of those years hands-on implementing AML, fraud or screening solutions.

  • Subject matter expertise in AML and compliance. You are familiar with key typologies and patterns, the regulatory expectations behind them, and how monitoring programmes as well as AI get examined.

  • You can confidently stand in front of an MLRO and discuss and defend a rule set. This is a must-have, not a nice-to-have.

  • Hands-on data skills: SQL, APIs, CSV and JSON, and data modelling. You're familiar with standardised payment message formats, including SWIFT MT and ISO 20022, SEPA and card data.

  • Integration literacy. You don't write production code, but you're at home with APIs, JSON payloads, SFTP configurations as well as SSO.

  • Proven track record of taking complex implementations to go-live on time, ideally several in parallel, with banking customers or other financial institutions.

  • Stakeholder alignment. You ensure that internal and external parties both have the information they need, keep them aligned and manage expectations.

  • Able to explain complexity simply. Imagine data models for compliance leads, fraud typologies for data engineers. You do it clearly in writing and in the room, in fluent English.

  • A degree in computer science, information systems, engineering, finance or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Bonus

  • Business-fluent German, for working with our DACH customers.

  • CAMS (or equivalent) certification, or time spent in a second-line compliance or MLRO team.

  • Builds constructive relationships with customers and stays calm and under pressure Builder mentality: works independently and brings structure to ambiguity where no established process exists, taking the initiative to define one.

  • Is a resourceful problem-solver who investigates unknowns and tests system behaviour. Knows when and whom to escalate.

  • Manages expectations proactively. Flags timeline and scope risks early, quantifies them, offers phased options and aligns Sales and Customer Success.

  • Handles product gaps transparently. Clarifies the underlying (regulatory) requirement, offers workarounds with their trade-offs, feeds back to Product and doesn't commit to unconfirmed dates .

  • You use AI tools such as Claude in your daily workflow to speed up mapping, documentation and analysis, and you have opinions about where they help and where they don't.

We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced Risk Manager to join our Project Controls team and play a key role supporting one of the UK’s largest and most complex infrastructure programmes.

Working as part of a major capital delivery environment, you will be responsible for supporting the effective identification, assessment and management of project risks across a complex programme of work. You will work closely with Project Controls, Planning, Commercial, Cost and Project Management teams to provide robust risk insight and help ensure that project decisions are informed by a clear understanding of uncertainty and exposure.

This is a project risk-focused role, rather than an enterprise or corporate risk position. The successful candidate will have strong experience of quantitative risk analysis, QSRA, cost and schedule risk analysis and project risk modelling, ideally gained within major construction, infrastructure, engineering or other complex capital programmes.

About us

CMR is first and foremost a team of people, passionate about the construction industry and changing the way project controls is provided.

We are a progressive and dynamic consultancy offering tailored project controls services across a range of industries.

Our Purpose (Why we exist): Inspiring new ways to help shape our construction industry.
Our Ambition (What we want to achieve): Re-imagine project controls through a digital lens, being the obvious choice for clients and the place to grow together with intention.

🔹 What’s in it for you?

  • At CMR you will have the opportunity to professionally develop like nowhere you have worked before.

  • If you demonstrate the capability, our merit-based system will enable you to develop quickly.

  • We use our in-house capability matrix to transparently track your progression and highlight development areas.

  • Join our small, dynamic team where every member has the chance to make a significant impact, shaping the future direction of our company and making a real difference.

  • We believe in rewarding our team for their achievements, celebrating our successes but equally helping each other when things are tough.

  • The opportunity to work on a major, nationally significant infrastructure programme, gaining exposure to some of the most complex project risk challenges in the UK.

🔹 You’ll

  • Lead and support the implementation of project risk management processes across complex infrastructure and construction projects.

  • Own and maintain project risk registers, ensuring risks are clearly defined in terms of causes, events, impacts, probability, consequence and mitigation actions.

  • Facilitate risk identification and review workshops with Project Management, Planning, Commercial, Engineering and other project stakeholders.

  • Challenge project teams to ensure risks are appropriately identified, assessed, quantified and actively managed.

  • Undertake and support Quantitative Schedule Risk Analysis (QSRA) and Quantitative Cost Risk Analysis (QCRA) to assess the potential impact of uncertainty on project outcomes.

  • Develop and maintain risk models, incorporating cost and schedule uncertainty, risk events, correlations and appropriate probability distributions.

  • Support the development and review of risk allowances, contingency and management reserves, ensuring these are supported by robust quantitative analysis.

  • Analyse project cost and schedule exposure and provide insight into P-values, confidence levels, ranges and potential outcomes.

  • Integrate risk information with project cost and schedule data to provide a consolidated view of project exposure.

  • Work closely with Planning and Project Controls teams to understand the relationship between risk, uncertainty, programme and critical path.

  • Monitor the effectiveness of mitigation strategies and assess changes in risk exposure over the project lifecycle.

  • Produce clear and concise risk reporting, dashboards and management information, highlighting key exposures, trends, emerging risks and areas requiring management intervention.

  • Provide risk input into project forecasts, baseline reviews, change management and key project decision-making processes.

  • Identify and analyse emerging risks and opportunities, ensuring these are captured and appropriately assessed.

  • Support the development of risk scenarios and sensitivity analysis to help project teams understand the potential impact of key uncertainties.

  • Maintain appropriate risk governance, ensuring risk data is accurate, auditable and aligned with project controls requirements.

  • Work collaboratively with Project Managers, Project Controls Leads, Planners, Commercial Managers, Cost Managers and senior client stakeholders.

  • Promote a proactive risk and uncertainty management culture, ensuring risk is used as a decision-making tool rather than simply a reporting requirement.

  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of CMR's project risk methodologies, processes, tools and ways of working.

  • Support Senior Risk Managers and Project Controls Leads in delivering high-quality risk management services to our clients.

🔹 We’re looking for:

Essential

  • Proven experience in a project risk management role within major construction, infrastructure, engineering or another complex capital project environment.

  • Strong understanding of project risk management methodologies and quantitative risk analysis.

  • Practical experience undertaking or supporting Quantitative Schedule Risk Analysis (QSRA).

  • Practical experience undertaking or supporting Quantitative Cost Risk Analysis (QCRA).

  • Experience developing, maintaining and interrogating project risk registers and risk models.

  • Strong understanding of the relationship between risk, cost, schedule, contingency and project forecasting.

  • Experience facilitating risk workshops with project and technical stakeholders.

  • Experience assessing probability, impact, uncertainty and risk exposure and translating this into meaningful project insight.

  • Strong analytical and numerical skills, with the ability to interpret complex project data and identify trends and areas of concern.

  • Good understanding of project controls and how risk interacts with planning, cost, commercial and change management.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to challenge assumptions and constructively influence project teams.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex quantitative analysis clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • A proactive approach to identifying emerging risks and opportunities and improving project performance.

  • Experience working in a complex, multi-stakeholder project environment.

Desirable

  • Experience working on major infrastructure, energy, nuclear, rail, defence or other highly regulated capital programmes.

  • Experience working on projects with significant levels of cost and schedule uncertainty.

  • Experience developing or reviewing Monte Carlo risk models.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Revenue Operations Manager to join our Revenue Operations team and act as a broad, senior partner to our revenue organisation. You'll run the complex analysis and modelling behind target setting and annual planning for the entire commercial organisation. You will also help the Director set and execute the revenue analytics strategy, and run the insights that shape how revenue leadership sees the business. As you ramp up, you will take on growing ownership of the forecasting cadence alongside the Director of Revenue Operations.

We are looking for someone with very strong analytical and modelling skills, which are the foundation of the role, especially in your first two quarters. Just as important, we want someone who is commercially minded and keen to grow into a generalist role, broadening from there into revenue insights and forecasting.


What You’ll Do

  • First 90 days: Scope the revenue analytics strategy and build the core dashboards.

  • First 180 days: Lead the analysis for the annual planning and target-setting cycle, and automate the core of revenue reporting and insights with AI tooling.

  • First 12 months: Take on co-ownership of the forecasting cadence with the Director of Revenue Operations.

 

What Will You Be Doing?

Run Complex Modelling & Analysis

  • Run complex analysis and modelling to support target setting and the annual planning process for the entire commercial organisation, made up of around 600 commercial roles across SDRs, AEs and Account Managers.

  • Build and maintain the models behind target setting: capacity, quota and productivity assumptions, and territory and segment allocation.

  • Frame the key planning questions, choose the method, pressure-test scenarios and sensitivities, and deliver clear recommendations to revenue leadership, explaining the trade-offs in plain language.

  • Work as the senior analytical partner to the other analyst on the team: stay hands-on in the models while setting the quality bar and documentation standards, so each planning cycle is repeatable and auditable.

Build the Revenue Analytics Strategy

  • Partner with the Director of Revenue Operations to define the revenue analytics strategy: what we need to build across Salesforce and Looker, and in what order.

  • Map the current reporting landscape — what exists, what's trusted, what's duplicated or out of date — and use that map to shape the build plan.

  • Own execution of that plan: build and maintain the core dashboards and reports that revenue leadership and the wider commercial organisation rely on.

  • Launch and run a recurring insights digest for revenue leaders, turning dashboards and data into a clear narrative — what changed, why it matters, what to do about it.

  • Bring a point of view on what's worth building versus what's noise, and be willing to push back on requests that don't earn their keep.

Grow Into Forecasting

  • Co-run the forecasting cadence with sales leaders and the Director of Revenue Operations — forecast calls, pipeline reviews, and accuracy tracking.

  • Build and refine forecasting models based on pipeline, productivity, and historical conversion.

  • Conduct strategic analyses to determine forecasting trends and identify opportunities for process improvement.


What You’ll Bring

  • Strong experience in Revenue or Sales Operations, preferably in a SaaS or technology company operating at a global or European level.

  • Advanced modelling and scenario analysis skills (spreadsheets and SQL), ideally with experience in target setting, capacity planning or annual planning for a large commercial organisation.

  • Solid Salesforce reporting skills and working fluency in a BI tool (Looker or equivalent), with a practical, business-first approach to data.

  • Commercial judgement and exposure to quota-carrying teams such as Account Executives, plus a generalist mindset: as comfortable building a dashboard as a planning model or running a forecasting call.

  • The ability to influence sales leadership and revenue executives, and to own ambiguous problems end to end, from framing the question to landing the recommendation.

  • Excellent written communication, since the insights digest is a core, ongoing deliverable of this role.

  • Hands-on experience using AI tools to automate analysis and reporting, or a clear appetite to build that skill quickly.


What We Offer

  • 25 days of annual leave to rest and recharge, plus all public holidays.

  • An optional pension scheme to support your long-term financial wellbeing.

  • A tax-efficient bike leasing scheme through Lease a Bike, for your commute or personal use.

  • Reimbursed commuting costs if you live more than 10km away from the office.

  • Competitive compensation paired with equity in Perk.

  • Unforgettable team experiences, including our annual summer party.

  • Comprehensive wellbeing support through Spring Health, offering fast access to 12 therapy and 12 coaching sessions for you and your loved ones.

  • Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave

  • 16 paid volunteer hours each year to give back to causes you care about.

  • Up to 20 “Work From Anywhere” days annually to explore the world while staying connected.

  • A fully paid four-week sabbatical after five years with Perk.

  • Relocation support to help you move seamlessly into one of our hubs.

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com, and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.
